questions.stem: A 24-year-old man with chronic diarrhea and abdominal pain also has recurrent shallow, painful ulcerations on his lips, buccal mucosa, and tongue, which he calls canker sores. These oral lesions are best described as which of the following?

explanation.summary: Aphthous ulcers of the oral mucosa, commonly called canker sores, may be a manifestation of Crohn disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because Crohn disease can affect any portion of the gastrointestinal tract, including the mouth and anus, patients may present with aphthous ulcers of the oral cavity. These are shallow, painful ulcerations occurring on the lips, cheeks, or tongue, and in the mouth an aphthous ulcer may be called a canker sore. Similar ulcers in the bowel can coalesce into linear, rake-like lesions.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A chancre is the painless ulcer of primary syphilis, whereas these lesions are painful and recurrent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A gumma is the granulomatous lesion of tertiary syphilis and is not the shallow mucosal ulcer described here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A mucocele is a mucus-filled cystic swelling of a salivary duct rather than a shallow painful ulceration.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A pseudomembrane is an adherent fibrinopurulent plaque of toxin-mediated colitis, not a shallow painful oral ulceration.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A pathologist describes a colonic biopsy from a patient with inflammatory bowel disease as showing ulceration with surrounding inflammation. Which histologic feature defines an ulcer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absence of the surface epithelial layer

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aggregation of histiocytes into a nodular collection

choices.label: C
choices.text: Full-thickness necrosis of the muscularis propria

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neutrophils filling the lumen of a colonic crypt

choices.label: E
choices.text: Separation of epithelium from its basement membrane

explanation.summary: Ulceration is defined histologically by loss of the surface epithelium, usually with accompanying inflammation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ulceration refers to the lack of surface epithelium at a site of injury, and it is often accompanied by inflammation as the tissue responds to the damage. Both Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis feature mucosal ulcerations.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A nodular collection of histiocytes is a granuloma, a separate finding that is the hallmark of Crohn disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Necrosis through the muscle layer describes a far deeper injury than the surface epithelial loss that defines an ulcer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neutrophils within a colonic gland constitute a crypt abscess, which marks active disease but is not an ulcer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Epithelial separation from the basement membrane describes a blister, such as the subepidermal blister of dermatitis herpetiformis.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man has an 8-year history of continuous colitis extending proximally from the rectum. He now reports pruritus and jaundice, and laboratory studies show a cholestatic pattern. Cholangiography demonstrates irregular strictures and dilations of the bile ducts. Which extraintestinal manifestation does he most likely have?

explanation.summary: Primary sclerosing cholangitis is an inflammatory disease of the bile ducts especially associated with ulcerative colitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both major forms of inflammatory bowel disease have extraintestinal manifestations. Primary sclerosing cholangitis is an inflammatory disease of the bile ducts that is especially associated with ulcerative colitis, and it produces cholestasis with the beaded duct irregularity seen on cholangiography.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This destructive condition of cartilage and joints affects the axial skeleton and would not produce cholestatic liver disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Inflammation of a portion of the eye is another extraintestinal manifestation but has no relationship to bile duct strictures.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Joint pain that moves from one area to another is a recognized manifestation but does not explain the biliary findings.
whyWrongByChoice.E: These painful, raised, ulcerative skin lesions are an extraintestinal manifestation but do not involve the biliary tree.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 41-year-old woman with a 6-year history of ulcerative colitis develops a painful, raised lesion on her left shin that rapidly ulcerates and has a violaceous, undermined border. Wound cultures are sterile. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Pyoderma gangrenosum is a painful, raised, ulcerative skin lesion particularly associated with ulcerative colitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Skin involvement is a recognized extraintestinal manifestation of inflammatory bowel disease. Pyoderma gangrenosum presents as painful, raised, ulcerative skin lesions and is especially associated with ulcerative colitis, although it is a non-specific finding that may be encountered in inflammatory bowel disease generally.

whyWrongByChoice.A: These shallow painful ulcerations occur on mucosal surfaces such as the lips, cheeks, and tongue rather than on the shin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This IgA-mediated blistering condition is tied to celiac disease and favors extensor surfaces, the upper back, and buttocks.
whyWrongByChoice.C: These tender subcutaneous nodules occur in both forms of inflammatory bowel disease but do not ulcerate in this fashion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A fulminant soft tissue infection would yield positive cultures and systemic toxicity rather than a sterile ulcer.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman with Crohn disease develops tender red nodules on both anterior shins. Three weeks earlier she had a febrile, bloody diarrheal illness after eating undercooked poultry. Which statement about this skin finding is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is specific for exposure to Clostridium difficile toxin

choices.label: B
choices.text: It may follow either Crohn disease or Campylobacter infection

choices.label: C
choices.text: It occurs in ulcerative colitis but not in Crohn disease

choices.label: D
choices.text: It reflects granulomatous inflammation of the bile ducts

choices.label: E
choices.text: It results from IgA antibodies cross-reacting with reticulin

explanation.summary: Erythema nodosum is seen in both Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis and may also follow Campylobacter infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Erythema nodosum is one of the skin manifestations of inflammatory bowel disease and, unlike pyoderma gangrenosum, is seen in both Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis. Campylobacter infections may also result in erythema nodosum, so either the underlying bowel disease or the recent enteritis could account for the nodules.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clostridium difficile causes toxin-mediated pseudomembranous colitis and is not the characteristic trigger for these nodules.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Erythema nodosum is not restricted to one form of the disease; it is seen in both Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bile duct inflammation describes primary sclerosing cholangitis, a separate extraintestinal manifestation of bowel disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: IgA cross-reactivity with reticulin produces the subepidermal blisters of dermatitis herpetiformis, not tender shin nodules.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man with ulcerative colitis reports a year of low back stiffness that is worst in the morning and improves with activity. Imaging shows fusion of both sacroiliac joints. Which extraintestinal manifestation of inflammatory bowel disease does he have?

explanation.summary: Ankylosing spondylitis, a destructive condition of cartilage and joints, is an extraintestinal manifestation of inflammatory bowel disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ankylosing spondylitis is a destructive condition of cartilage and joints and is among the extraintestinal manifestations of both Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis. Its sacroiliac involvement with inflammatory back pain matches this presentation, and it shares the HLA-B27 association seen with inflammatory bowel disease-associated arthritis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: This manifestation is joint pain that moves from one area to another rather than a fixed, fusing axial arthropathy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This is an inflammatory disease of the bile ducts and would present with cholestasis rather than sacroiliac fusion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This disorder is a post-infectious triad of arthritis, urethritis, and conjunctivitis, and no preceding infection is described.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This is inflammation of a portion of the eye and does not account for back stiffness or sacroiliac joint changes.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman with Crohn disease develops a red, painful right eye with photophobia and blurred vision. Slit-lamp examination shows cells and flare in the anterior chamber. Which of the following best identifies this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conjunctivitis, as seen in reactive arthritis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uveitis, inflammation of part of the eye

explanation.summary: Uveitis, inflammation of a portion of the eye, is a recognized extraintestinal manifestation of inflammatory bowel disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Uveitis is listed among the extraintestinal manifestations of both Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis, alongside primary sclerosing cholangitis, ankylosing spondylitis, migratory polyarthritis, and skin involvement. Anterior chamber cells and flare indicate intraocular inflammation rather than a surface process.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conjunctival inflammation is part of the post-infectious reactive arthritis triad and does not produce anterior chamber cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Erythema nodosum produces tender nodules on the shins and is not an eyelid or intraocular process.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Herpetic eye disease affects the cornea and conjunctiva and is not the listed extraintestinal manifestation of bowel disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Yellowing of the sclera reflects hyperbilirubinemia from cholestatic liver disease rather than intraocular inflammation.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman with chronic diarrhea has colonic biopsies showing granulomatous inflammation. Before Crohn disease is accepted as the diagnosis, infectious and systemic causes of granulomas are considered. Which of the following characteristically produces granulomatous inflammation?

explanation.summary: Fungal infections such as Histoplasma capsulatum, along with tuberculosis, tertiary syphilis, and sarcoidosis, feature granulomatous inflammation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Granulomatous inflammation is characteristic of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection, in which the granulomas caseate, of many fungal infections such as Histoplasma capsulatum, of Treponema pallidum in the form of tertiary syphilitic gummas, and of sarcoidosis, a disease of unknown etiology. These must be excluded before granulomas are attributed to Crohn disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This organism produces toxins that damage the gastrointestinal tract and form pseudomembranes, but it does not cause granulomas.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This organism causes bloody diarrhea through toxin production and does not generate granulomatous inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This protozoan damages the small-bowel brush border and causes malabsorption without granuloma formation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This virus causes a self-limited gastroenteritis and is not associated with granulomatous inflammation.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man develops copious watery diarrhea 5 days after finishing a course of clindamycin. Colonoscopy shows adherent yellow-white plaques scattered over the colonic mucosa. Which mechanism best explains the mucosal injury?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Destruction of the duodenal and jejunal brush border

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immune cross-reaction between gliadin and enterocytes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Invasion of the lamina propria with mesenteric node spread

explanation.summary: Clostridium difficile produces toxins that damage the gastrointestinal tract and form pseudomembranes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clostridium difficile is the cause of pseudomembranous colitis. It produces toxins that damage the gastrointestinal system, and the resulting injury generates the adherent plaques seen at colonoscopy. It does not cause granulomatous inflammation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Brush border destruction describes Giardia infection, which produces greasy malabsorptive stools without pseudomembranes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nodular histiocyte aggregates are the hallmark of Crohn disease and are not produced by this toxin-mediated colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cross-reaction with a dietary grain protein describes celiac disease, which injures the duodenum rather than forming plaques.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mucosal invasion with proliferation in the lamina propria and mesenteric nodes describes Campylobacter, which causes fever and dysentery.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man returns from international travel with fever, abdominal cramps, and bloody diarrhea. Stool culture grows a curved, gram-negative rod, and stool microscopy shows abundant leukocytes. Which of the following best explains his fever?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A toxin absorbed from contaminated water without mucosal invasion

choices.label: B
choices.text: Loss of the brush border of the duodenum and jejunum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Preformed toxin released from food held at room temperature

choices.label: D
choices.text: Proliferation within the lamina propria and mesenteric lymph nodes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Shearing of red blood cells across glomerular microthrombi

explanation.summary: Campylobacter jejuni invades the mucosa, and fever results from proliferation in the lamina propria and mesenteric lymph nodes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Campylobacter jejuni is a common cause of traveler's diarrhea and food poisoning, acting through toxin production and other virulence factors. Bloody diarrhea, or dysentery, appears when the organism invades the mucosa, and fever results from bacterial proliferation within the lamina propria and the mesenteric lymph nodes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Toxin action without mucosal invasion describes enterotoxigenic E. coli, which causes watery rather than bloody diarrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Brush border loss causes malabsorption with fatty stools and would not produce fever with bloody diarrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Preformed toxin ingestion produces abrupt vomiting and diarrhea without the invasive, febrile, bloody picture described.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Red cell shearing across microthrombi is the mechanism of hemolytic uremic syndrome, a complication of Shiga-like toxin.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: Three weeks after a diarrheal illness caused by Campylobacter jejuni, a 24-year-old man who carries the HLA-B27 allele develops joint pain, painful urination, and red, light-sensitive eyes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Reactive arthritis is the post-infectious triad of arthritis, urethritis, and conjunctivitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Reactive arthritis is a classic triad of arthritis, urethritis, and conjunctivitis that arises from the immune response to infections such as Campylobacter, Salmonella, and Chlamydia trachomatis, particularly in patients carrying HLA-B27. Joint pain, painful urination, and light-sensitive eyes correspond to the three components.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This destructive condition of cartilage and joints affects the axial skeleton and does not include urethritis and conjunctivitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is a skin finding of tender nodules and does not explain arthritis, urethritis, or conjunctivitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This post-Campylobacter complication produces paralysis from demyelination rather than a triad of joint, urinary, and eye findings.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This is joint pain that moves from one area to another and does not account for the urinary and ocular symptoms.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man develops arthritis, urethritis, and conjunctivitis several weeks after an episode of Campylobacter enteritis. Which genetic factor most increases susceptibility to this complication?

explanation.summary: Reactive arthritis after enteric infection occurs particularly in patients with the HLA-B27 allele.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with the HLA-B27 genotype may develop reactive arthritis as a result of Campylobacter infection. The same allele is associated with inflammatory bowel disease-associated arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This class II allele presents gliadin peptides and is associated with celiac disease rather than post-infectious arthritis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This allele is associated with Goodpasture syndrome and systemic lupus erythematosus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This allele is associated with rheumatoid arthritis, a chronic symmetric polyarthritis rather than a post-infectious triad.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This is the other class II allele associated with celiac disease and has no role in reactive arthritis.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: Two weeks after a self-limited Campylobacter jejuni diarrheal illness, a 30-year-old man develops symmetric ascending weakness of the legs with loss of deep tendon reflexes. Nerve conduction studies show demyelination. Which mechanism best explains his paralysis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibodies to lipopolysaccharide cross-react with neural gangliosides

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autoantibodies to acetylcholine receptors block neuromuscular transmission

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bacterial exotoxin blocks acetylcholine release at the motor endplate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Direct viral invasion and destruction of anterior horn motor neurons

choices.label: E
choices.text: Immune complexes deposit within the endoneurial microvasculature

explanation.summary: Guillain-Barre syndrome after Campylobacter reflects molecular mimicry between bacterial lipopolysaccharide and neural gangliosides.
explanation.whyCorrect: Guillain-Barre syndrome, also called acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy, results from molecular mimicry to infectious antigens in predisposed individuals. After Campylobacter jejuni infection, antibodies against lipopolysaccharide cross-react with gangliosides of the nervous system, causing demyelination, or loss of the insulating myelin coat surrounding axons, and paralysis follows from impaired nerve signaling.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Antibodies against the acetylcholine receptor cause fatigable weakness without the demyelination seen here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Toxin-mediated blockade of acetylcholine release describes botulism, which is not the post-Campylobacter complication described.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Destruction of anterior horn cells by a virus is a different mechanism and would not produce demyelination on nerve conduction studies.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Immune complex deposition in vessels is not the described mechanism of this post-infectious demyelinating polyneuropathy.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man develops ascending paralysis from acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy following Campylobacter enteritis. Which pair of interventions most directly targets the self-reacting antibodies responsible for his deficits?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gluten withdrawal and oral iron replacement

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oral azithromycin and intravenous fluid resuscitation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral metronidazole and fecal microbiota transfer

explanation.summary: Plasmapheresis removes the self-reacting antibodies of Guillain-Barre syndrome, and IVIG neutralizes their effects.
explanation.whyCorrect: Plasmapheresis is a method of removing self-reacting antibodies, and administration of intravenous immunoglobulin is a strategy for neutralizing the effects of those antibodies. Both are possible interventions in Guillain-Barre syndrome, in which antibodies raised against bacterial lipopolysaccharide cross-react with neural gangliosides.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antiviral therapy and lowering immunosuppression address viral colitis in immunosuppressed patients, not this neuropathy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Removing a dietary antigen and replacing iron addresses celiac disease and its malabsorption, not an antibody-mediated neuropathy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antibiotics and fluids address the enteric infection itself and do nothing about antibodies already cross-reacting with nerve.
whyWrongByChoice.D: These measures target Clostridium difficile colitis and have no role in a post-infectious demyelinating polyneuropathy.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman with Guillain-Barre syndrome after Campylobacter infection is admitted to the intensive care unit with progressive weakness. Her family asks about the expected course. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Demyelination spares the respiratory muscles in nearly all cases

choices.label: B
choices.text: Recovery is immediate once antibiotics eradicate the organism

choices.label: C
choices.text: The axons are transected and are unable to remyelinate at all

choices.label: D
choices.text: The deficit is permanent and progresses to a spastic paralysis

choices.label: E
choices.text: The disease usually resolves, but respiratory failure can be fatal

explanation.summary: Guillain-Barre syndrome is generally self-resolving, but respiratory failure can cause death and some patients need weeks of intensive care.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although the disease is self-resolving, death from respiratory failure can occur, and some patients spend weeks in the intensive care unit. The paralysis arises from demyelination with impaired nerve signaling rather than permanent structural loss, which is why recovery is the rule when patients are supported through the acute illness.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Respiratory involvement is precisely the danger, and it is the cause of death when this illness proves fatal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Eradicating the organism does not reverse antibodies that are already cross-reacting with neural gangliosides.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The lesion is loss of the insulating myelin coat rather than transection of the underlying axons.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The weakness of this demyelinating polyneuropathy is typically transient rather than permanent and spastic.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman develops abrupt watery, non-bloody diarrhea 2 days into a trip abroad, after drinking untreated local water. The stools are watery rather than greasy or foul-smelling, she is afebrile, and stool studies show no blood and no leukocytes; the mucosa is not invaded. Which organism is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Enterotoxigenic E. coli causes traveler's diarrhea through toxins, without invading the mucosa.
explanation.whyCorrect: Enterotoxigenic E. coli is a common cause of traveler's diarrhea. It does not actively invade the mucosa; instead it releases toxins, and disease follows ingestion of contaminated food or water. The absence of blood, fever, and fecal leukocytes fits a non-invasive, toxin-mediated illness.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This organism invades the mucosa and proliferates in the lamina propria and mesenteric nodes, producing fever and dysentery.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This virus causes colitis in immunosuppressed patients rather than an acute watery illness in a healthy traveler.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This strain is an important cause of bloody diarrhea through toxin production, and the stools here contain no blood.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This protozoan damages the small-bowel brush border and produces fatty, greasy, foul-smelling stools from malabsorption.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy develops bloody diarrhea 3 days after eating an undercooked hamburger. Stool culture grows Escherichia coli O157:H7. His parents ask why he is not being given an antibiotic. Which of the following is the best explanation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Killing the bacteria releases toxin and raises hemolytic uremic syndrome risk

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are inactivated by gastric acid before reaching the colonic mucosa

choices.label: C
choices.text: They cannot reach an organism that proliferates within mesenteric lymph nodes

choices.label: D
choices.text: They select for Clostridium difficile overgrowth and pseudomembranous colitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: They worsen the malabsorption that follows destruction of the brush border

explanation.summary: Antibiotics are avoided in enterohemorrhagic E. coli because killing the organism can release more toxin and precipitate hemolytic uremic syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Enterohemorrhagic E. coli, particularly the O157:H7 strain, causes bloody diarrhea through toxin production. Antibiotics are not recommended because killing the bacteria could release even more toxin and increase the risk of hemolytic uremic syndrome.

whyWrongByChoice.B: These agents are not rendered ineffective by gastric acid; the issue is the consequence of killing the organism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This strain acts through toxin rather than by proliferating in mesenteric lymph nodes, so access is not the problem.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Antibiotic-associated Clostridium difficile colitis is a real concern in general, but it is not the reason antibiotics are withheld here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Malabsorption from brush border loss is the mechanism of Giardia infection and is unrelated to this toxin-mediated illness.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: Five days after the onset of bloody diarrhea caused by Escherichia coli O157:H7, a 6-year-old girl has pallor, decreased urine output, and a serum creatinine of 2.8 mg/dL. The peripheral blood smear shows fragmented red blood cells. Which mechanism best explains these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibodies to lipopolysaccharide cross-react with gangliosides of nerves

choices.label: B
choices.text: Granulomatous inflammation of glomeruli obstructs the capillary tufts

choices.label: C
choices.text: Loss of the intestinal brush border leads to malabsorption and greasy stools

choices.label: D
choices.text: Shiga-like toxin injures endothelium, forming microthrombi that shear cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Toxin-induced mucosal necrosis produces an adherent fibrinous pseudomembrane

explanation.summary: In hemolytic uremic syndrome, Shiga-like toxin damages endothelium, producing microthrombi that shear red cells and cause kidney failure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hemolytic uremic syndrome is a microangiopathic hemolytic anemia. In E. coli O157:H7 infection, the Shiga-like toxin damages endothelium, including that of the glomeruli, leading to thrombosis from platelet activation and aggregation. Red cells are sheared into schistocytes as they pass through the microthrombi, and kidney failure follows.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cross-reaction with neural gangliosides produces Guillain-Barre syndrome after Campylobacter, not anemia with renal failure.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Granulomatous inflammation is not the mechanism of renal failure following this toxin-mediated infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Brush border destruction causes fatty malabsorptive stools and has no bearing on hemolysis or renal injury.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An adherent fibrinopurulent membrane is the lesion of Clostridium difficile colitis and does not cause red cell fragmentation.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A peripheral blood smear from a 5-year-old with hemolytic uremic syndrome shows numerous fragmented red blood cells, described as schistocytes. This process is best classified as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aplastic anemia from failure of marrow stem cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia from warm IgG antibodies

choices.label: C
choices.text: Iron deficiency anemia from chronic occult blood loss

choices.label: D
choices.text: Megaloblastic anemia from impaired nuclear DNA synthesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia from intravascular shearing

explanation.summary: Schistocytes indicate microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, in which red cells are sheared by microthrombi within vessels.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hemolytic uremic syndrome is a microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, meaning red blood cells are sheared into schistocytes as they pass through microthrombi formed within vessels. The thrombi follow toxin-mediated endothelial damage with platelet activation and aggregation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Marrow failure produces pancytopenia with a hypocellular marrow and does not generate fragmented red cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Antibody-mediated red cell destruction produces spherocytes rather than the mechanical fragmentation described here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chronic blood loss produces small, pale red cells rather than the sheared fragments of an intravascular process.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Impaired DNA synthesis produces large oval red cells and hypersegmented neutrophils, not fragmented cells.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 30-year-old hiker who drank from an unfiltered mountain stream has 3 weeks of bloating and fatty, greasy, foul-smelling stools that float. He has no fever and no blood in the stool. Which organism is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Giardia lamblia, acquired from contaminated unfiltered water, damages the small-bowel brush border and causes malabsorptive fatty stools.
explanation.whyCorrect: Giardia lamblia, also known as Giardia duodenalis, is a flagellated protozoan commonly present in contaminated, unfiltered water. It damages the brush border of the duodenum and jejunum, an important component of nutrient absorption, so fatty, greasy, foul-smelling stools result from malabsorption.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This organism causes febrile, often bloody diarrhea from mucosal invasion rather than a malabsorptive fatty stool.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This organism produces pseudomembranous colitis after antibiotic exposure, with watery rather than greasy stools.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This virus causes colitis in immunosuppressed patients and is not a cause of malabsorption in a healthy hiker.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This strain causes bloody diarrhea through toxin production and may be complicated by hemolytic uremic syndrome.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: Stool examination in a 28-year-old with several weeks of bloating and greasy stools shows flagellated organisms whose trophozoite form has been likened to a stingray or a falling leaf, along with oval cysts. Which mechanism best explains this patient's diarrhea?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It damages the brush border of the duodenum and jejunum

choices.label: B
choices.text: It elaborates a toxin that produces adherent colonic pseudomembranes

choices.label: C
choices.text: It forms large intranuclear inclusions within colonic endothelium

choices.label: D
choices.text: It invades the mucosa and proliferates in mesenteric lymph nodes

choices.label: E
choices.text: It triggers IgA antibodies that cross-react with dermal reticulin

explanation.summary: Giardia exists as cysts and flagellated trophozoites and causes malabsorption by damaging the duodenal and jejunal brush border.
explanation.whyCorrect: Giardia lamblia demonstrates both cyst and trophozoite forms, the trophozoite resembling a stingray or a falling leaf, and both can be identified in stool samples. The organism damages the brush border of the duodenum and jejunum, and because the brush border is an important component of nutrient absorption, malabsorption with fatty, greasy, foul-smelling stools results.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Adherent fibrinopurulent plaques are the lesion of Clostridium difficile colitis, a toxin-mediated disease of the colon.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Large intranuclear inclusions indicate cytomegalovirus colitis, typically encountered in immunosuppressed patients.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mucosal invasion with spread to mesenteric nodes describes Campylobacter jejuni, which produces fever and bloody diarrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.E: IgA cross-reactivity with reticulin produces dermatitis herpetiformis in celiac disease, not a protozoal malabsorption.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman with ulcerative colitis taking immunomodulating therapy has worsening diarrhea despite escalation of her usual regimen. Colonic biopsies show numerous enlarged cells containing large intranuclear inclusions surrounded by a clear halo, resembling an owl's eye. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Owl's eye intranuclear inclusions in a colonic biopsy indicate cytomegalovirus colitis, which is common in patients with ulcerative colitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cytomegalovirus is a double-stranded DNA virus of the human herpesvirus family that can affect the colon, and such infection is commonly seen in patients with ulcerative colitis. Identification of numerous viral inclusions described as resembling an owl's eye is an indication for antiviral treatment in such patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This virus is listed among the ordinary viral causes of infectious diarrhea and does not produce these inclusions.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This organism produces toxin-mediated pseudomembranes rather than viral cytopathic changes within cell nuclei.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The cytopathic changes of this virus are multinucleation, nuclear molding, and chromatin margination, not owl's eye inclusions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This virus causes a self-limited gastroenteritis without the characteristic intranuclear inclusion bodies described.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 39-year-old man on immunosuppression after renal transplantation has bloody diarrhea. Colonoscopy shows ulceration and necrosis that closely mimic inflammatory bowel disease. Biopsy shows multinucleation, nuclei conforming to one another, and a dark rim of chromatin at the nuclear edge. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Multinucleation, nuclear molding, and chromatin margination are the classic cytopathic changes of herpes simplex virus colitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Herpes simplex virus colitis may be seen in immunocompromised patients, and treatment should be started to prevent morbidity and mortality. Ulcerations and necrosis occur that can mimic inflammatory bowel disease. The classic viral cytopathic changes are chromatin margination, seen as a dark purple rim at the edge of the nucleus, nuclear molding in which nuclei conform to one another, and multinucleation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This organism causes toxin-mediated pseudomembranous colitis without changes within the nuclei of infected cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This diagnosis rests on nodular histiocyte aggregates and transmural inflammation, not on viral cytopathic nuclear changes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This infection is identified by numerous large intranuclear inclusions resembling an owl's eye rather than molded multinucleated cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This protozoan damages the small-bowel brush border and causes malabsorption rather than colonic ulceration and necrosis.

questions.topicName: Immune-related and Infectious Causes of Diarrhea

questions.stem: A 47-year-old woman reports several months of fatigue and generalized itching. Physical exam is unremarkable except for mild scratch marks. Laboratory studies show a markedly elevated serum alkaline phosphatase with only mild transaminase elevation. Serologic testing is positive for anti-mitochondrial antibodies. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Anti-mitochondrial antibodies with a cholestatic (high alkaline phosphatase) picture in a middle-aged woman indicate primary biliary cholangitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is an autoimmune destruction of small and medium intrahepatic bile ducts with a 9:1 female predominance peaking at 40-50 years. Diagnosis rests on elevated alkaline phosphatase, supportive histology, and anti-mitochondrial antibodies (AMA), which are present in about 95% of cases. Early symptoms are fatigue and pruritus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autoimmune hepatitis is associated with ANA, anti-smooth muscle actin, and anti-LKM-1 antibodies, not AMA, and produces a hepatitic (high transaminase) rather than a purely cholestatic pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chronic hepatitis C produces anti-HCV antibodies and detectable HCV RNA, not anti-mitochondrial antibodies.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Primary sclerosing cholangitis is associated with p-ANCA and predominantly affects men with ulcerative colitis, not AMA-positive women.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia is a laboratory classification of elevated bilirubin, not a specific antibody-associated disease.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man with a 5-year history of ulcerative colitis develops fatigue, pruritus, and intermittent jaundice. Alkaline phosphatase is elevated. Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography shows a characteristic beaded appearance of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts with strictures alternating with dilated segments. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: A man with ulcerative colitis and beaded bile ducts on cholangiography has primary sclerosing cholangitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) causes inflammation and obliterative fibrosis of extrahepatic and large intrahepatic bile ducts, producing strictures with dilation of preserved segments. It occurs mostly in men in the 3rd to 5th decades and has a strong association with inflammatory bowel disease (70%), particularly ulcerative colitis. The gold-standard finding is beading of the ducts on ERCP/MRCP.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autoimmune hepatitis is a hepatocellular disease with interface hepatitis, not an obliterative fibrosing disease of the bile ducts.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chronic hepatitis C causes portal lymphoplasmacytic inflammation of the parenchyma and is diagnosed by HCV RNA PCR, not by biliary beading.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Choledocholithiasis produces a discrete obstructing stone, not diffuse multifocal strictures and beading throughout the biliary tree, and is not linked to ulcerative colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Primary biliary cholangitis attacks small intrahepatic ducts, has a 9:1 female predominance, and is diagnosed with AMA rather than by ductal beading on cholangiography.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman is evaluated for fatigue and anorexia. She has a history of autoimmune thyroiditis. Laboratory studies show markedly elevated AST and ALT and an elevated serum IgG. Liver biopsy shows inflammation and hepatocellular injury at the interface between the portal tract and parenchyma with numerous plasma cells in clusters. Which of the following autoantibodies is most likely to be positive?

explanation.summary: Interface hepatitis with plasma cells and high IgG in a young woman with another autoimmune disease is autoimmune hepatitis, associated with anti-smooth muscle actin antibodies.
explanation.whyCorrect: Autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) is a chronic progressive hepatitis with female predominance, elevated serum IgG, and histologic interface inflammation with clusters of plasma cells. Its typical autoantibodies are ANA, anti-smooth muscle actin (SMA, type I), and anti-LKM-1 (type II). Anti-SMA is more specific for AIH than the nonspecific ANA.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anti-centromere antibody is associated with limited systemic sclerosis (CREST), not autoimmune hepatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Anti-HCV antibody indicates hepatitis C, which classically shows portal lymphoplasmacytic inflammation rather than the interface pattern with high IgG and autoimmune associations.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Anti-mitochondrial antibody characterizes primary biliary cholangitis, a cholestatic bile duct disease, not the interface hepatitis described here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: p-ANCA is associated with primary sclerosing cholangitis and vasculitis, not with plasma-cell-rich interface hepatitis.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 41-year-old man with a history of intravenous drug use has fatigue and persistently elevated transaminases documented over the past 8 months. You suspect chronic viral hepatitis. Which of the following is the best test to demonstrate active infection?

choices.label: C
choices.text: HCV RNA by polymerase chain reaction

explanation.summary: HCV RNA by PCR is the best early test to confirm active hepatitis C infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hepatitis C virus usually presents as a chronic infection with persistently elevated transaminases for more than 6 months and is spread parenterally, including via IV drug use. Diagnosis involves PCR testing for HCV RNA, which is the best early test demonstrating active infection, along with serologic testing for anti-HCV antibodies.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anti-HCV IgG indicates exposure but cannot distinguish active from past infection; a positive antibody with negative PCR reflects prior, cleared infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Anti-mitochondrial antibody is a marker of primary biliary cholangitis and has no role in diagnosing hepatitis C.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Alkaline phosphatase is a marker of cholestatic bile duct disease such as PBC or PSC, not a test for active HCV replication.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serum IgG supports autoimmune hepatitis and does not demonstrate active viral replication.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A liver biopsy from a 50-year-old woman with cholestatic liver disease shows a portal tract markedly expanded by lymphocytes and plasma cells surrounding a destructive granulomatous reaction centered on a bile duct. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: A granulomatous reaction destroying a bile duct (the florid duct lesion) is characteristic of primary biliary cholangitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The characteristic histology of PBC is lymphocytic and/or granulomatous destruction of small and medium intrahepatic bile ducts. The classic florid duct lesion is a portal tract expanded by lymphocytes and plasma cells around a destructive granulomatous reaction centered on a bile duct, matching this biopsy in a middle-aged woman.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alcoholic hepatitis shows steatosis, Mallory-Denk bodies, and neutrophilic infiltration, not granulomatous bile duct destruction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Autoimmune hepatitis shows interface hepatitis with plasma cells attacking hepatocytes, not a granulomatous reaction centered on a bile duct.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chronic hepatitis C shows portal lymphoplasmacytic inflammation with fibrosis of the parenchyma, without bile-duct-centered granulomas.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primary sclerosing cholangitis shows periductal onion-skin concentric fibrosis, not a granulomatous florid duct lesion.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A liver biopsy from a patient with a cholestatic bile duct disorder shows a degenerating bile duct entrapped within a dense concentric layer of fibrosis described as an onion-skin pattern. Which of the following diseases does this finding most strongly suggest?

explanation.summary: The onion-skin concentric periductal fibrosis is the hallmark histology of primary sclerosing cholangitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: In primary sclerosing cholangitis there is periductal inflammation in the portal tracts that leads to fibrosis (sclerosis) of the smaller bile ducts. The classic histologic finding is a degenerating bile duct entrapped in a dense onion-skin concentric scar, which progresses to stenosis of biliary ducts with dilation of segments behind the obstruction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autoimmune hepatitis shows interface inflammation with plasma cells, not periductal onion-skin scarring.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chronic hepatitis C shows portal lymphoplasmacytic inflammation and bridging fibrosis on trichrome, not onion-skin duct scarring.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hepatic amyloidosis shows amorphous eosinophilic deposits that stain with Congo red, not periductal concentric fibrosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Primary biliary cholangitis shows a granulomatous florid duct lesion, not concentric onion-skin periductal fibrosis.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 9-year-old girl presents with acute hepatitis and is found to have autoimmune hepatitis. Testing reveals a specific autoantibody more commonly seen in the pediatric form of this disease. Which of the following autoantibodies was most likely detected?

explanation.summary: Anti-LKM-1 defines type II autoimmune hepatitis, which is more common in children.
explanation.whyCorrect: Autoimmune hepatitis autoantibodies include ANA, anti-smooth muscle actin (type I), and anti-LKM-1 (anti-liver kidney microsome-1). Anti-LKM-1 antibodies mark type II AIH and are noted to be more common in children, making them the expected finding in this pediatric case.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anti-dsDNA antibody is specific for systemic lupus erythematosus, not for autoimmune hepatitis subtypes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Anti-HCV antibody indicates hepatitis C infection, not autoimmune hepatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Anti-mitochondrial antibody characterizes primary biliary cholangitis, a disease of middle-aged women, not pediatric autoimmune hepatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: p-ANCA is associated with primary sclerosing cholangitis and vasculitis, not type II AIH.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: During evaluation of a patient with suspected primary biliary cholangitis, anti-mitochondrial antibodies are found to be positive. Which of the following statements best describes the diagnostic value of this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AMA is elevated in about 95% of PBC patients

choices.label: B
choices.text: AMA is entirely specific for PBC and never appears in other conditions

choices.label: C
choices.text: AMA is present in only a small subset of PBC cases and is usually absent

choices.label: D
choices.text: AMA is the confirmatory test for primary sclerosing cholangitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: AMA titer correlates directly with the severity of bile duct destruction

explanation.summary: AMA is highly sensitive for PBC (about 95%) but is not perfectly specific, appearing in lupus and autoimmune hepatitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: A diagnosis of PBC combines elevated serum alkaline phosphatase, characteristic histology, and anti-mitochondrial antibodies. AMA are elevated in 95% of patients with PBC but can also be seen in lupus and autoimmune hepatitis, so the diagnosis rests on the overall clinical, biochemical, and histologic picture.

whyWrongByChoice.B: AMA is not entirely specific; it can appear in lupus and autoimmune hepatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: AMA is present in the large majority (about 95%) of PBC cases, not a small subset.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The confirmatory approach for PSC is cholangiography (ERCP/MRCP), not AMA testing.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The brick does not describe AMA titer as a direct measure of severity; diagnosis relies on the combined clinical picture.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A patient with primary sclerosing cholangitis is being discussed at a conference. A proposed mechanism of bile duct injury in this disease is described. Which of the following best represents this mechanism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anti-mitochondrial antibodies directly lyse biliary epithelial cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Copper accumulation causing oxidative bile duct injury

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deposition of immune complexes within hepatocyte cytoplasm

choices.label: D
choices.text: Direct viral cytopathic destruction of bile ducts by hepatitis C

choices.label: E
choices.text: T cells activated in the damaged colonic mucosa migrate to the liver

explanation.summary: In PSC, T cells activated in inflamed ulcerative colitis mucosa are proposed to migrate to the liver and cross-react with a bile duct antigen.
explanation.whyCorrect: PSC has a genetic component (first-degree relatives at increased risk, association with HLA-B8) and a strong link to inflammatory bowel disease. A proposed mechanism is that T cells activated in the damaged mucosa of patients with ulcerative colitis migrate to the liver and cross-react with a bile duct antigen, driving the biliary injury.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anti-mitochondrial antibodies are the marker of primary biliary cholangitis, and the brick does not describe them causing direct lysis in PSC.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Copper accumulation describes Wilson disease, not the T-cell cross-reactivity mechanism proposed for PSC.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Immune complex deposition in hepatocytes is not the described mechanism of PSC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PSC is not caused by direct hepatitis C viral cytopathic destruction; that describes a different, viral process.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man is found to have positive anti-HCV IgG antibodies on routine screening. Follow-up HCV RNA polymerase chain reaction testing is negative. Which of the following best explains these results?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A false-positive requiring anti-mitochondrial antibody testing

choices.label: B
choices.text: Active, actively replicating hepatitis C infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Past hepatitis C infection that has resolved

explanation.summary: Positive anti-HCV IgG with negative HCV RNA PCR indicates a past, resolved hepatitis C infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diagnosis of HCV uses PCR for HCV RNA to demonstrate active infection and serologic testing for anti-HCV antibodies. Positive anti-HCV IgG antibodies with a negative HCV PCR indicate past infection, because antibodies persist after the virus has been cleared.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The pattern is the expected serologic signature of resolved infection, not a false positive needing AMA testing.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Active replication would show a positive HCV RNA PCR, but the PCR here is negative.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Autoimmune hepatitis is diagnosed by autoantibodies and elevated IgG, not by anti-HCV antibodies.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primary biliary cholangitis is diagnosed by AMA and cholestatic labs and is unrelated to anti-HCV serology.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman presents with acute onset nausea, vomiting, and jaundice progressing to confusion. Laboratory studies show markedly elevated liver transaminases consistent with acute liver failure. Autoimmune hepatitis is suspected. According to the diagnostic approach for this disease, which combination of features best establishes the diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A positive HCV RNA polymerase chain reaction plus anti-HCV antibodies

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autoantibodies, elevated serum IgG, exclusion of other causes, and supportive biopsy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Beading of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts plus p-ANCA positivity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Elevated alkaline phosphatase plus a positive anti-mitochondrial antibody titer

choices.label: E
choices.text: Isolated unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with normal transaminases and a normal serum IgG

explanation.summary: AIH is diagnosed by combining autoantibodies, elevated serum IgG, exclusion of other etiologies, and supportive histology.
explanation.whyCorrect: A diagnosis of autoimmune hepatitis rests on the combination of four features: the presence of autoantibodies, elevation of serum IgG, exclusion of other etiologies such as viral hepatitis and drugs, and supportive histologic findings on liver biopsy. AIH can present acutely with life-threatening liver failure and markedly elevated transaminases, as in this patient.

whyWrongByChoice.A: HCV RNA PCR and anti-HCV antibodies diagnose hepatitis C, which must actually be excluded to diagnose AIH.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ductal beading and p-ANCA point to primary sclerosing cholangitis, not autoimmune hepatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Elevated alkaline phosphatase and AMA define primary biliary cholangitis, a cholestatic disease, not autoimmune hepatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Isolated unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with normal transaminases is not the hepatitic picture of autoimmune hepatitis.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A medical student is reviewing why jaundice is an important physical finding. Which of the following statements best describes the pathophysiologic basis of jaundice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blue discoloration of the extremities caused by deoxygenated hemoglobin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bronze skin pigmentation caused by iron overload

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pallor caused by reduced red blood cell mass

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reddening of the palms caused by elevated estrogen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Yellow discoloration of skin caused by elevated bilirubin

explanation.summary: Jaundice is yellow discoloration of skin, sclera, and mucous membranes due to elevated bilirubin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Jaundice is a yellow discoloration of the skin, sclera, and mucous membranes caused by elevated bilirubin, and it may indicate serious underlying pathology. Hyperbilirubinemia can be classified into unconjugated and conjugated types, each with different causes, including the infectious and inflammatory liver diseases covered in this brick.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blue discoloration from deoxygenated hemoglobin describes cyanosis, not jaundice.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bronze pigmentation from iron overload describes hemochromatosis, not the bilirubin-driven yellowing of jaundice.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pallor from reduced red cell mass describes anemia, not jaundice.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Palmar erythema from elevated estrogen is a sign of chronic liver disease but is not the definition of jaundice.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman of Northern European ancestry is diagnosed with autoimmune hepatitis after evaluation of elevated transaminases, a positive anti-smooth muscle actin antibody, and interface hepatitis on biopsy. Her physician explains that the disease has a known genetic predisposition. Which of the following HLA associations is most strongly linked to autoimmune hepatitis in her population?

explanation.summary: Autoimmune hepatitis in Caucasian populations is strongly associated with HLA-DR3.
explanation.whyCorrect: AIH has a known genetic predisposition with strong HLA associations that differ by population: HLA-DR3 in the Caucasian population, HLA-DR4 in the Japanese population, and HLA-DRB1 in the South American population. In a patient of Northern European ancestry, HLA-DR3 is the expected association.

whyWrongByChoice.A: HLA-DRB1 is the AIH association described in the South American population, not the Caucasian population.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HLA-DR4 is the AIH association described in the Japanese population, not the Caucasian population.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HLA-B8 is the antigen associated with primary sclerosing cholangitis, not autoimmune hepatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HLA-B27 is not among the HLA associations described for autoimmune hepatitis.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman is diagnosed with autoimmune hepatitis after a work-up for fatigue and elevated transaminases. She asks what will happen if she declines treatment. Which of the following best describes the expected natural history of untreated disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complete resolution once the inciting viral trigger has cleared

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion to a cholestatic pattern with progressive bile duct loss

choices.label: C
choices.text: Progression to end-stage liver disease or death in most patients

choices.label: D
choices.text: Spontaneous and durable remission in the majority of patients

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stable mild transaminase elevation without progression to fibrosis

explanation.summary: Untreated autoimmune hepatitis leads to death or progresses to cirrhosis in the majority of cases.
explanation.whyCorrect: Autoimmune hepatitis is a chronic, progressive hepatitis. The degree of fibrosis increases with disease progression, and untreated disease leads to death or progresses to end-stage liver disease (cirrhosis) in a majority of cases. This is why the disease, although rare, accounts for 3-5% of liver transplants and why a therapeutic response to immunosuppression is a defining feature.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Triggers such as viral infections are proposed initiators, but the disease is a self-sustaining chronic progressive process rather than one that resolves when a trigger clears.
whyWrongByChoice.B: AIH is a hepatocellular disease with interface inflammation; conversion to a bile-duct-destroying cholestatic disease is not its natural history.
whyWrongByChoice.D: AIH does not remit spontaneously in most patients; it is described as chronic and progressive.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fibrosis increases with disease progression rather than remaining stable and absent.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes mellitus is found to have elevated AST and ALT, elevated serum IgG, positive antinuclear and anti-smooth muscle actin antibodies, and interface hepatitis on liver biopsy. Viral hepatitis and drug causes have been excluded. Which of the following therapeutic responses is characteristic of her disease?

explanation.summary: Autoimmune hepatitis is defined in part by a therapeutic response to immunosuppression.
explanation.whyCorrect: This patient meets the four diagnostic features of autoimmune hepatitis (autoantibodies, elevated IgG, exclusion of other etiologies, supportive histology), and her coexisting type 1 diabetes fits the association of AIH with other autoimmune conditions. AIH is described as a chronic, progressive hepatitis associated with genetic predisposition, autoantibodies, and a therapeutic response to immunosuppression.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antiviral therapy addresses viral hepatitis, which has already been excluded in this patient.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Biliary stenting addresses obstructive duct disease such as the strictures of primary sclerosing cholangitis, not hepatocellular autoimmune inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Copper chelation treats Wilson disease, not autoimmune hepatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Phlebotomy treats iron overload, not an autoimmune hepatocellular disease.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man has routine laboratory testing the morning after completing his first marathon. Serum AST is markedly elevated, while ALT is only minimally elevated. He has no jaundice, abdominal pain, or history of liver disease. Which of the following best explains the elevated AST?

explanation.summary: AST is not liver-specific; an isolated AST elevation may reflect muscle damage rather than liver disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: ALT (alanine transaminase) is an enzyme found in the liver that is released into the bloodstream when the liver is damaged. AST (aspartate transaminase) helps the body break down amino acids, and an increase in AST may mean liver damage, liver disease, or muscle damage. A marked AST rise with only minimal ALT change after strenuous exercise points to muscle as the source.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autoimmune hepatitis produces elevation of both AST and ALT (elevated transaminases) along with autoantibodies and elevated IgG, not an isolated AST rise after exertion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cholestatic bile duct disease such as PBC or PSC is marked by elevated alkaline phosphatase, not an isolated AST elevation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chronic hepatitis C causes persistent elevation of serum transaminases over months, not a sudden isolated AST rise in a healthy man after a race.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Impaired bilirubin conjugation causes unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, which would not explain an elevated transaminase.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman with Hashimoto thyroiditis has persistently elevated transaminases and an elevated serum IgG. Viral hepatitis serologies are negative and she takes no medications. Liver biopsy shows interface hepatitis with clusters of plasma cells. ANA, anti-smooth muscle actin, and anti-LKM-1 antibodies are all negative. Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoimmune hepatitis is excluded because autoantibodies are absent

choices.label: B
choices.text: Primary biliary cholangitis is the most likely diagnosis given her thyroiditis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Repeat viral testing is required because negative serology cannot exclude hepatitis C

choices.label: D
choices.text: Seronegative autoimmune hepatitis remains likely based on the overall picture

choices.label: E
choices.text: The biopsy findings indicate steatohepatitis rather than autoimmune disease

explanation.summary: Autoantibodies may be absent in a small subset of AIH cases (seronegative autoimmune hepatitis), so diagnosis rests on overall clinical, serologic, and histologic features.
explanation.whyCorrect: Typical AIH autoantibodies (ANA, anti-SMA, anti-LKM-1) may not be present in a small subset of cases, termed seronegative autoimmune hepatitis. Because titers do not correlate well with severity or outcome and antibodies can be absent, it is important to make the diagnosis based on the overall clinical, serologic, and histologic features. This woman has elevated IgG, an associated autoimmune condition, exclusion of viral and drug causes, and classic interface hepatitis with plasma cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Absent autoantibodies do not exclude AIH; a small subset of cases are seronegative.
whyWrongByChoice.B: PBC is a cholestatic bile duct disease diagnosed by elevated alkaline phosphatase, anti-mitochondrial antibodies, and granulomatous duct destruction, none of which is present here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Viral hepatitis has already been excluded by negative serologies; the negative autoantibodies do not create a need to re-test for HCV.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Interface hepatitis with clusters of plasma cells is the typical pathology of autoimmune hepatitis, not steatohepatitis.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man with a remote history of intravenous drug use has chronically elevated transaminases. HCV RNA PCR is positive. As part of the evaluation, antinuclear antibodies and anti-smooth muscle actin antibodies are also found to be positive. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoantibodies can occur in chronic viral hepatitis and do not establish autoimmune hepatitis here

choices.label: B
choices.text: Combined positivity confirms an overlap syndrome of primary biliary cholangitis and hepatitis C

choices.label: C
choices.text: He has autoimmune hepatitis, and the positive HCV RNA result is an incidental finding

choices.label: D
choices.text: The height of the autoantibody titers indicates severe disease requiring urgent transplant listing

choices.label: E
choices.text: The positive PCR result is a false positive caused by the cross-reacting autoantibodies

explanation.summary: AIH autoantibodies may appear in other disease processes such as chronic viral hepatitis, so they cannot make the diagnosis of AIH when viral hepatitis is present.
explanation.whyCorrect: Autoantibodies such as ANA and anti-SMA also may be present in other disease processes such as steatohepatitis and chronic viral hepatitis (e.g., with HBV and HCV). A diagnosis of AIH requires exclusion of other etiologies including viral hepatitis, and this patient has active hepatitis C demonstrated by positive HCV RNA PCR. The autoantibodies therefore do not establish AIH.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Primary biliary cholangitis is associated with anti-mitochondrial antibodies and a cholestatic picture, neither of which is described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: AIH cannot be diagnosed without excluding viral hepatitis, and this patient has active HCV infection with a compatible parenteral exposure history.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Autoantibody titers do not correlate well with disease severity or outcome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HCV RNA PCR detects viral RNA and is the best early test demonstrating active infection; autoantibodies do not cause a false-positive PCR.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 48-year-old woman with long-standing dry eyes and dry mouth attributed to Sjogren syndrome develops fatigue and generalized itching. Laboratory studies show an elevated serum alkaline phosphatase with mildly elevated transaminases. Which of the following liver diseases is most strongly associated with her underlying condition?

explanation.summary: Primary biliary cholangitis is associated with other autoimmune conditions including Sjogren syndrome, thyroiditis, systemic sclerosis, and celiac disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: PBC is an autoimmune disease with a 9:1 female predominance peaking at 40-50 years, and it is associated with other autoimmune conditions including Sjogren syndrome, thyroiditis, systemic sclerosis, and celiac disease. This woman's early symptoms of fatigue and pruritus with elevated alkaline phosphatase fit the early presentation of PBC.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alcoholic hepatitis is a toxic injury, not an autoimmune disease associated with Sjogren syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.B: AIH is associated with type 1 diabetes, thyroiditis, and celiac sprue and presents with a hepatitic (transaminase-predominant) rather than cholestatic (alkaline phosphatase-predominant) picture.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hepatitis C is spread parenterally or sexually and is not an autoimmune association of Sjogren syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PSC is strongly associated with inflammatory bowel disease (70% of patients), especially ulcerative colitis, and occurs mostly in men.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman with primary biliary cholangitis asks how her immune system damages her liver. Which of the following best describes the pathogenic mechanism of bile duct injury in this disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct viral cytopathic injury to biliary epithelium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Eosinophil-mediated injury of the extrahepatic bile duct

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immune complex deposition in the hepatic sinusoids

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neutrophil-mediated suppurative destruction of large bile ducts

choices.label: E
choices.text: T-lymphocyte-mediated attack on small interlobular bile ducts

explanation.summary: PBC is a T-lymphocyte-mediated attack on small interlobular bile ducts.
explanation.whyCorrect: As with other autoimmune conditions, a combination of genetic predisposition and an environmental trigger (infections, toxic chemical exposure) contributes to the development of PBC, which is a T-lymphocyte-mediated attack on small interlobular bile ducts. This produces the characteristic lymphocytic and/or granulomatous destruction of small and medium-sized intrahepatic bile ducts.

whyWrongByChoice.A: PBC is autoimmune, not a viral cytopathic process.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The extrahepatic bile duct is the territory of PSC, and PBC injury is lymphocytic rather than eosinophilic.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Immune complex deposition in sinusoids is not the described mechanism of PBC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PBC targets small and medium intrahepatic ducts via lymphocytes and granulomas, not large ducts via neutrophils.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 53-year-old woman was diagnosed with primary biliary cholangitis 8 years ago after presenting with fatigue and pruritus. At a follow-up visit she now has scleral icterus and a palpable spleen tip. Which of the following best characterizes these new findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Evidence that the diagnosis was actually primary sclerosing cholangitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Expected early manifestations that precede pruritus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Findings unrelated to her liver disease

choices.label: D
choices.text: Manifestations of a superimposed acute viral hepatitis

explanation.summary: In PBC, fatigue, pruritus, and right upper quadrant pain are early symptoms, whereas splenomegaly and jaundice are seen with advanced disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Early on, patients with PBC present with fatigue, pruritus, and right upper quadrant abdominal pain. Splenomegaly and jaundice are seen with advanced disease, and later stages can progress to liver cirrhosis (chronic liver scarring and poor function). The appearance of jaundice and splenomegaly years after an early presentation therefore signals progression.

whyWrongByChoice.A: PSC and PBC share overlapping symptoms; jaundice and splenomegaly indicate advanced disease in either and do not change the diagnosis of an AMA-established PBC.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Jaundice and splenomegaly are late findings; the early manifestations are fatigue, pruritus, and right upper quadrant pain.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Splenomegaly and jaundice are specifically listed as features of advanced PBC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nothing in the scenario suggests a new viral exposure; these findings are the described progression of PBC itself.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman with no symptoms is found on routine screening labs to have an elevated serum alkaline phosphatase. Transaminases and bilirubin are normal. She takes no medications. Which of the following is the most appropriate next test to evaluate for the likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: An increasing number of PBC cases are detected in asymptomatic patients with elevated alkaline phosphatase; anti-mitochondrial antibody testing is the key serologic step.
explanation.whyCorrect: An increasing number of PBC cases are being detected in asymptomatic patients with elevated serum alkaline phosphatase levels. The diagnosis of PBC is established by a combination of elevated serum alkaline phosphatase, characteristic histology, and the presence of anti-mitochondrial antibodies, which are elevated in 95% of patients. In a middle-aged woman (peak incidence 40-50 years, 9:1 female predominance), AMA testing is the appropriate next step.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anti-LKM-1 is a marker of type II autoimmune hepatitis, which is more common in children and produces a hepatitic picture.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HCV RNA PCR evaluates viral hepatitis, which presents with persistently elevated transaminases rather than an isolated alkaline phosphatase elevation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ceruloplasmin evaluates Wilson disease, not the cholestatic autoimmune duct disease suggested here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serum IgG supports autoimmune hepatitis, a hepatocellular disease with elevated transaminases, not an isolated cholestatic enzyme elevation.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 49-year-old woman with primary biliary cholangitis confirmed by anti-mitochondrial antibodies and a florid duct lesion on biopsy is found to also have a positive antinuclear antibody. Which of the following best describes the significance of this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ANA is elevated in about half of PBC patients and does not change the diagnosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: ANA is never found in PBC and indicates a laboratory error

choices.label: C
choices.text: ANA positivity indicates coexisting primary sclerosing cholangitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: ANA positivity indicates the patient has autoimmune hepatitis instead of PBC

choices.label: E
choices.text: ANA positivity means the AMA result was a false positive

explanation.summary: In addition to AMA (95%), antinuclear antibodies are also elevated in about 50% of PBC cases.
explanation.whyCorrect: AMA are elevated in 95% of patients with PBC, and in 50% of cases antinuclear antibodies (ANA) are also elevated. ANA is a nonspecific autoantibody seen in a variety of autoimmune conditions, so its presence in a patient with established PBC is expected in roughly half of cases and does not alter the diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: ANA is elevated in about 50% of PBC cases, so it is a common rather than impossible finding.
whyWrongByChoice.C: PSC patients may have elevated ANA, but ANA positivity does not diagnose PSC; PSC requires characteristic beading of the bile ducts on ERCP/MRCP.
whyWrongByChoice.D: ANA is not specific for AIH and is found in about half of PBC patients; this patient's AMA, cholestatic picture, and florid duct lesion establish PBC.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A positive ANA does not invalidate AMA; both antibodies commonly coexist in PBC.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A pathologist is comparing two autoimmune cholestatic diseases. In primary biliary cholangitis, which portion of the biliary tree is the target of inflammatory destruction?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Large intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts

choices.label: E
choices.text: Small and medium-sized intrahepatic bile ducts

explanation.summary: PBC destroys small and medium-sized intrahepatic bile ducts, whereas PSC affects extrahepatic and large intrahepatic ducts.
explanation.whyCorrect: Primary biliary cholangitis is an autoimmune disease characterized by inflammatory destruction of small and medium-sized intrahepatic bile ducts, mediated by a T-lymphocyte attack on small interlobular bile ducts. This contrasts with PSC, which is characterized by inflammation and obliterative fibrosis of extrahepatic and large intrahepatic bile ducts.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The ampulla is not the site of PBC's inflammatory destruction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Extrahepatic duct involvement characterizes PSC, not PBC.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The gallbladder and cystic duct are not the target of PBC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Large intrahepatic and extrahepatic ducts are the territory of primary sclerosing cholangitis.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 42-year-old man with ulcerative colitis and primary sclerosing cholangitis diagnosed 10 years ago presents with hematemesis, abdominal distension with a fluid wave, and new confusion. Which of the following best describes his current status?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute autoimmune hepatitis superimposed on the underlying PSC

choices.label: B
choices.text: An acute ulcerative colitis flare requiring urgent colectomy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Choledocholithiasis obstructing the common bile duct

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cirrhosis from PSC progression, which requires liver transplant

choices.label: E
choices.text: The typical early presentation of primary sclerosing cholangitis

explanation.summary: With progression, 15-25% of PSC patients develop cirrhosis with esophageal bleeding, ascites, and confusion, and these patients require a liver transplant.
explanation.whyCorrect: The most common presenting symptoms of PSC are fatigue, pruritus, and jaundice, and nearly half of patients are asymptomatic with elevated alkaline phosphatase. With progression, 15%-25% of those with PSC develop liver cirrhosis, with accompanying esophageal bleeding, ascites, and confusion. These patients require a liver transplant.

whyWrongByChoice.A: AIH presents with markedly elevated transaminases and autoantibodies; this triad reflects decompensated cirrhosis from PSC progression.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hematemesis, ascites, and confusion are manifestations of liver cirrhosis, not of a colitis flare.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A common duct stone would cause obstructive jaundice and pain, not the ascites and confusion of cirrhosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Early PSC presents with fatigue, pruritus, and jaundice, or is asymptomatic with elevated alkaline phosphatase; esophageal bleeding, ascites, and confusion are late.

questions.topicName: Infectious/Inflammatory Causes of Jaundice

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man whose father has primary sclerosing cholangitis asks whether he is at risk. Which of the following best reflects what is known about the etiology of this disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: First-degree relatives are protected because of shared HLA-DR3 alleles

choices.label: B
choices.text: First-degree relatives have an increased risk, and there is an association with HLA-B8

choices.label: C
choices.text: The disease has no genetic component and arises purely from bile duct stones

choices.label: D
choices.text: The disease is caused by chronic hepatitis C infection acquired within families

choices.label: E
choices.text: The disease is transmitted in an autosomal dominant fashion with full penetrance

explanation.summary: PSC has a genetic component: first-degree relatives are at increased risk and there is an association with HLA-B8.
explanation.whyCorrect: First-degree relatives of patients with PSC have an increased risk of developing the disease, suggesting a genetic component, and there is an association with certain HLA antigens (HLA-B8). A proposed mechanism of injury is that T cells activated in the damaged mucosa of ulcerative colitis migrate to the liver and cross-react with a bile duct antigen.
